page: Google Cloud Platform g2-standard-4 is a graphics-optimized virtual machine belonging to the g2 family. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores of an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.2 GHz, utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The CPU configuration includes 32 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 38 MB L3 cache, with support for AVX, AVX512F, and AVX512_VNNI instruction sets. The instance is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB per core, and does not include local storage or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

The defining feature of the g2-standard-4 is its integrated NVIDIA L4 GPU, based on the Ada Lovelace architecture, which provides 24 GB of dedicated VRAM. This hardware accelerator shifts the performance profile of the server. While general-purpose CPU and memory benchmarks—such as stress-ng, Geekbench, and Passmark—fall into the bottom 25% tier, the GPU delivers top-tier performance for machine learning workloads. Specifically, LLM inference benchmarks for a medium 7B model show prompt processing speeds of 2296.42 tokens per second and text generation speeds of 52.18 tokens per second.

The server presents a clear architectural tradeoff: it pairs a modest, lower-performing CPU host system with a highly capable modern GPU. Consequently, it is not cost-efficient for CPU-bound tasks, database operations, or standard web serving, where its benchmarks remain weak. However, for GPU-accelerated workloads like small-to-medium large language model inference, graphics rendering, and machine learning pipeline stages, the resource density of the NVIDIA L4 GPU provides high qualitative cost efficiency. It is best suited for AI inference, light model training, and CUDA-accelerated data processing.
